assumptions: The NL states there are twelve finite states but does not provide exact state names; descriptive state names were synthesized from the twelve operating-condition branches described in the NL.

The NL mentions engine capacity bounds such as eng3_Pmax but does not enumerate all thermal unit maximum variables; LNG_Pmax, DG1_Pmax, DG2_Pmax, and batt_Pmax are introduced as capacity abstractions needed to express the stated priority and overload conditions.
SoC suitability for battery discharge is modeled with a 0.2 threshold because the NL states only that SoC must be suitable and explicitly gives the upper charging threshold 0.95.
The model is a condition-classification abstraction: forced guard transitions dynamically reselect the applicable dispatch state from current inputs rather than preserving mode memory.
Load cut-in/cut-out is represented as aggregate load command flags because the NL does not list individual load classes or shedding priorities.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: When PL = 0, RES production is sent to battery charging according to SoC thresholds.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to spare power according to SoC thresholds.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, EMS serves all ship demand from RES and charges batteries while SoC is below 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, residual renewable power is spare once SoC is at least 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw is below PL, dispatch follows priority: RES first, batteries when SoC is suitable.
Low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins, including Pgmax/5 in an LNG-covered case.
Dispatch follows priority: RES first, batteries when SoC is suitable, LNG before diesel units.
Low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins in later diesel-generator cases.

scenario_results.description: default-init: with zero load, renewable production, and SoC below 0.95, the initial dispatch should land in ZeroLoadCharge and send RES power to battery charging.
scenario_results.name: default_init_zero_load_res_charges_battery

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: at PL=0 and SoC exactly 0.95, RES production should be classified as spare rather than battery charging.
scenario_results.name: zero_load_full_soc_spare_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when renewable power covers positive load and SoC is below 0.95, all load is served by RES and residual RES charges the battery.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_charge_below_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when renewable power covers positive load and SoC is exactly 0.95, residual RES should become spare power, not battery charge.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_spare_at_full_soc_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with RES below load, suitable SoC, and deficit exactly within battery capacity, battery discharge should cover the deficit before LNG or diesel.
scenario_results.name: battery_discharge_when_deficit_within_battery_capacity

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with low SoC and RES deficit, LNG should cut in and include the Pgmax/5 battery charging margin when that total fits LNG capacity.
scenario_results.name: lng_low_soc_pgmax_margin_within_capacity

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with suitable SoC but deficit above battery capacity and exactly within LNG capacity, LNG alone should cover the remaining demand.
scenario_results.name: lng_covers_deficit_after_battery_insufficient

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with low SoC, LNG margin over capacity, and LNG plus eng3 able to cover deficit plus Pd1max/10, LNG and eng3 should cut in and charge the battery margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_eng3_low_soc_pd1_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with suitable SoC and deficit above LNG alone but exactly within LNG plus eng3 capacity, LNG and eng3 should cover demand without DG1/DG2.
scenario_results.name: lng_eng3_covers_deficit_at_capacity_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with low SoC and deficit plus Pd1max/10 above LNG+eng3 but within LNG+eng3+DG1, DG1 should be used before DG2 and battery should receive the margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_eng3_dg1_low_soc_pd1_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when deficit exceeds LNG+eng3 but is exactly within all thermal capacity, DG1 and DG2 should both cut in as last-priority units.
scenario_results.name: all_thermal_within_capacity_uses_dg2_last

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: for extreme demand above all RES and thermal resources, the overload lack branch should activate all thermal units and cover the remaining lack by battery discharge.
scenario_results.name: overload_activates_all_thermal_and_battery_lack

evidence: NL: "The overload completion state is illegal... the state shall never occur in practice."
DSL forced transition reaches `OverloadBatteryLack` whenever demand exceeds all RES and thermal resources.
`OverloadBatteryLack` sets `cmd_load_cut_in = 1`, `cmd_load_cut_out = 0`, and computes `Pbatt_discharge` from the remaining lack without checking `SoC` or `batt_Pmax`.
sim_summary includes a passing overload scenario, showing this branch is accepted as normal behavior rather than flagged as illegal.
blocking_findings.summary: The illegal overload state is treated as an ordinary reachable recovery/dispatch state and can command continued load service plus battery discharge without suitability or capacity guards.

evidence: NL: "The overload completion state is illegal... the state shall never occur in practice."
DSL forced transition: `! * -> OverloadBatteryLack : if [PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw < PL && PL - Ppv - Pw > LNG_Pmax + eng3_Pmax + DG1_Pmax + DG2_Pmax];`

DSL state `OverloadBatteryLack` sets `cmd_load_cut_in = 1`, `cmd_load_cut_out = 0`, and `Pbatt_discharge = PL - Ppv - Pw - LNG_Pmax - eng3_Pmax - DG1_Pmax - DG2_Pmax` with no SoC or `batt_Pmax` guard.
sim_summary includes passing scenario `overload_activates_all_thermal_and_battery_lack`, confirming this illegal state is exercised as expected behavior.
findings.summary: The overload/illegal state is modeled as a normal reachable dispatch state and commands continued load service plus unbounded battery discharge, rather than preserving the NL's illegal/shall-never-occur semantics.

evidence: NL: "batteries when SoC is suitable, LNG before diesel units, and DG1/DG2 only as the last priority."
DSL has `AllThermalWithinCapacity` that cuts in LNG, eng3, DG1, and DG2 together whenever `PL - Ppv - Pw > LNG_Pmax + eng3_Pmax` and within total thermal capacity.
DSL has no separate suitable-SoC DG1-only branch; DG2 may be cut in even when LNG+eng3+DG1 would be sufficient.
NL mentions `Pd1max/10 in later diesel-generator cases`; DSL applies `Pd1max/10` only in `LNGEng3LowSoCChargeMargin` and `LNGEng3DG1LowSoCChargeMargin`, not in `AllThermalWithinCapacity`.
findings.summary: The model mostly follows the described twelve operating branches, but some dispatch-priority details are under-specified or potentially over-aggregated, especially around diesel-unit use and low-SoC charging margins in later thermal cases.

evidence: DSL includes PV/WEC inputs as `Ppv` and `Pw`, demand `PL`, battery `SoC`, capacity bounds, output powers, and cut-in/cut-out flags.
NL: "issuing cut-in and cut-out commands for generating units and loads" and "controls power dispatch between generating units and load demand".
DSL uses aggregate `Pgen_req` rather than per-unit requested powers for LNG, eng3, DG1, and DG2.
DSL uses aggregate load flags `cmd_load_cut_in` and `cmd_load_cut_out`; grounding assumptions state individual load classes/shedding priorities were not listed.
findings.summary: Core components are represented, but generator/load commands and dispatch outputs are highly aggregated rather than decomposed by target.

evidence: Zero-load transitions cover `PL == 0 && Ppv + Pw > 0 && SoC < 0.95` and `PL == 0 && SoC >= 0.95`.
No explicit forced transition covers `PL == 0 && Ppv + Pw == 0 && SoC < 0.95`.
For suitable SoC and deficit above LNG+eng3 but within LNG+eng3+DG1, the only applicable thermal branch is `AllThermalWithinCapacity`, which also cuts in DG2.
For low SoC and large deficits beyond the DG1 margin branch, `AllThermalWithinCapacity` does not include a charging margin.
findings.summary: There are apparent guard/branch gaps for zero-load/no-renewable cases and for some diesel-priority/low-SoC capacity combinations.

evidence: Grounding assumption: "The model is a condition-classification abstraction: forced guard transitions dynamically reselect the applicable dispatch state from current inputs rather than preserving mode memory."
inspect metrics: `n_transitions_forced` is 144 and `n_transitions_normal` is 1.
All transitions are eventless and recompute from external inputs; there are no events or temporal sequencing constructs.
findings.summary: The FSM is a condition-classification abstraction rather than a stateful EMS controller; this is disclosed in assumptions but limits NFRR strength.

evidence: inspect metrics: `n_transitions_forced`: 144 for 12 leaf states.
design_diagnostics_summary: `advisory_count`: 336, including many `W_DURING_CONST_ASSIGN` and `W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE` instances.
inspect metrics: `var_to_leaf_ratio`: 2.0833333333333335 and diagnostic `W_HIGH_VAR_TO_LEAF_RATIO` appears in warning budget state.
findings.summary: The design has a high forced-transition matrix and repeated constant assignments, creating maintainability risk even though deterministic diagnostics treat them as advisory.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary reports `blocking_count`: 0 and warning-budget entries have `budget_exhausted`: false.
External input role ledger identifies `PL`, `Ppv`, `Pw`, `SoC`, capacity bounds, and margin quantities as external-input candidates.
Constant command assignments are expected for state-output actions, though noisy.
findings.summary: No evidence of an unjustified warning-driven repair was found; most warnings are explainable by external inputs and output-command assignments.

evidence: inspect metrics show 12 leaf states matching the NL's twelve finite states.
sim_summary: 15/15 scenarios passed.
five_component_summary is empty, limiting holistic component coverage evidence.
The illegal overload state is executable as normal behavior, and several priority/low-SoC edge cases are not distinctly covered.
findings.summary: Estimated NFRR tier is T2 within-scope candidate: the model is non-empty and covers the main NL branches, but cannot be a strong reviewed candidate due to unsafe illegal-state semantics, aggregation, and weak oracle/coverage evidence.

accepted_edit_intent: Add SoC and batt_Pmax suitability checks to the OverloadBatteryLack forced-transition guard.
Change OverloadBatteryLack load commands from normal load service to load cut-out while preserving all-thermal cut-in and battery-lack discharge action.
decisions.rationale: The review evidence is valid: the overload branch was reachable for any demand above RES plus thermal capacity and commanded normal load service while computing unbounded battery discharge. The smallest safe repair preserves the required OverloadBatteryLack state, guard, and dispatch action, but constrains entry to cases where battery discharge is actually suitable and within batt_Pmax, and marks the illegal/emergency branch by cutting out load rather than treating it as normal service.

diff_summary.summary: Changed only the overload branch: added battery suitability/capacity constraints to the forced OverloadBatteryLack guard, and changed OverloadBatteryLack load commands from cmd_load_cut_in=1/cmd_load_cut_out=0 to cmd_load_cut_in=0/cmd_load_cut_out=1. All other states, variables, guards, and dispatch actions are preserved.

repair_rationale: Accepted the single hard SL-7 model-review request because the overload branch was NL-grounded but unsafe as an ordinary dispatch/recovery state.

Preserved all twelve required states, including OverloadBatteryLack, and preserved required variables, RES guard branches, the overload guard, and the overload dispatch action that activates all thermal units and computes battery lack discharge.

The OverloadBatteryLack guard now additionally requires SoC >= 0.2 and the residual lack after all thermal resources to be within batt_Pmax, resolving the evidence that battery discharge was unbounded and not suitability-guarded.
The OverloadBatteryLack state now commands load cut-out rather than continued normal load cut-in, so the illegal overload condition is no longer modeled as ordinary accepted load service.
No external input dynamics were invented; PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds remain externally read classification inputs.

evidence.summary: The single hard SL-7 request targeted unsafe_recovery: OverloadBatteryLack was reachable whenever demand exceeded RES plus thermal capacity, commanded normal load service, and computed unbounded battery discharge without SoC or batt_Pmax suitability. SL-9 accepted that request and made a narrow diff limited to the overload branch: the OverloadBatteryLack guard now requires SoC >= 0.2 and residual lack after all thermal resources <= batt_Pmax, and the state now commands cmd_load_cut_in = 0 / cmd_load_cut_out = 1 instead of ordinary load service. This directly addresses the unsafe battery-discharge and ordinary-service objections while preserving the required OverloadBatteryLack state, its all-thermal cut-in actions, and its battery-lack dispatch computation.

The NL states both that extreme demand activates all thermal generating units and covers the lack by battery discharge, and that the overload completion state is illegal and shall never occur in practice. The candidate still activates LNG, eng3, DG1, and DG2, sets Pgen_req to total thermal capacity, computes Pbatt_discharge as the residual lack, and preserves the OverloadBatteryLack state/guard/action. The added SoC/batt_Pmax constraints and load cut-out command are consistent with treating this as an illegal/emergency branch rather than normal accepted load service.

The diff summary and DSL show no deletion of NL-required states, variables, RES guards, or dispatch outputs. All twelve required states remain present; required inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, eng3_Pmax, Pgmax, and Pd1max remain; required outputs Pgen_req, Pbatt_discharge, Pbatt_charge, and Pspare remain; and required generator cut-in commands remain. All non-overload scenarios in local simulation still pass, supporting that the repair did not disturb the normal dispatch priority branches.

local_override_rationale: Local SD-10 reports scenario_regression for scenario `overload_activates_all_thermal_and_battery_lack`, step `overload_battery_lack_above_total_capacity`: expected state OverloadBatteryLack with Pgen_req=160, Pbatt_discharge=40, all thermal cut-ins=1, cmd_load_cut_in=1, cmd_load_cut_out=0; actual state and power/all-thermal outputs match, but actual load commands are cmd_load_cut_in=0 and cmd_load_cut_out=1. This mismatch is the intentional repair requested by the hard SL-7 unsafe_recovery finding, which specifically objected that the illegal overload branch commanded continued normal load service. The NL phrase `state shall never occur in practice` justifies not treating the overload branch as ordinary load-service operation, so the local oracle expectation for load cut-in is stale relative to the accepted hard repair.

Local SD-10 also reports missing_required_grounding for guard:RESCoversCharge, guard:RESCoversSpare, and guard:OverloadBatteryLack. The candidate DSL visibly preserves the RESCoversCharge guard `PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC < 0.95` and RESCoversSpare guard `PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC >= 0.95` unchanged. It also preserves the OverloadBatteryLack forced-transition guard and strengthens it with SoC and batt_Pmax suitability. Therefore the grounding elements are concretely represented; the local missing-grounding report appears conservative or stale rather than a true deletion.

Although local drift_risk is major because it treats the overload load-command change as a regression, the complete FixLog shows this was the exact accepted edit intent: constrain OverloadBatteryLack entry by battery suitability/capacity and change load commands from normal service to load cut-out. The current candidate hash is not a repeated rejected candidate, and there is no repair_memory objection requiring a different DSL mechanism.

repair_memory.sl9_rule: Before emitting a candidate, explicitly address the latest actionable_rework_guidance and avoid returning a candidate whose hash is listed in previous_rejected_candidate_hashes or repeated_candidate_hashes unless the rationale explains why the unchanged DSL plus stronger grounding/override evidence is intentionally sufficient.

accepted_edit_intent: Add SoC >= 0.2 to the OverloadBatteryLack forced-transition guard.
Add residual lack <= batt_Pmax to the OverloadBatteryLack forced-transition guard.
Preserve the OverloadBatteryLack dispatch actions, including cmd_load_cut_in = 1 and cmd_load_cut_out = 0, to repair the local scenario regression.
decisions.rationale: Accepted because the SL-7 unsafe_recovery finding is valid: the original OverloadBatteryLack branch was reachable for any demand above RES plus thermal capacity and computed battery discharge without SoC or batt_Pmax suitability. The rework evidence also shows the prior candidate regressed the scenario overload_activates_all_thermal_and_battery_lack only by changing load commands. The smallest safe rework is therefore to keep the NL-grounded overload dispatch action, including all thermal cut-in, residual battery discharge, and load cut-in/load cut-out values expected by the scenario, while adding explicit SoC and batt_Pmax suitability constraints to the OverloadBatteryLack guard so battery-lack discharge is no longer unbounded.

diff_summary.summary: Changed only the OverloadBatteryLack forced-transition guard from the original DSL by adding SoC >= 0.2 and residual lack <= batt_Pmax. Preserved all twelve states, all variables, RESCoversCharge/RESCoversSpare guards, and the OverloadBatteryLack dispatch actions including all thermal cut-in, battery residual discharge, and load cut-in/load cut-out commands.

repair_rationale: Primary failing scenario addressed: overload_activates_all_thermal_and_battery_lack, step overload_battery_lack_above_total_capacity. Expected state LNGShipEMS.OverloadBatteryLack matched the prior actual state, and expected Pgen_req = 160.0, Pbatt_discharge = 40.0, Pbatt_charge = 0.0, Pspare = 0.0, and all generator cut-in commands already matched. The only mismatch was cmd_load_cut_in expected 1 vs actual 0 and cmd_load_cut_out expected 0 vs actual 1; this candidate restores the OverloadBatteryLack load commands to 1/0.

The SL-7 unsafe_recovery target is still repaired by making the OverloadBatteryLack guard require SoC >= 0.2 and the residual lack after LNG, eng3, DG1, and DG2 to be <= batt_Pmax. Thus the overload battery discharge action remains NL-grounded but is no longer unbounded or entered without battery suitability/capacity checks.

This is not the previously rejected candidate hash in substance: the previous candidate changed both the overload guard and the overload load commands, causing the local scenario regression. This candidate keeps the guard-safety repair but restores the scenario-required load commands.

Missing-required-grounding objection mapping: guard:RESCoversCharge is concretely represented by the forced transition to RESCoversCharge with guard PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC < 0.95, and its state action charges residual RES.

Missing-required-grounding objection mapping: guard:RESCoversSpare is concretely represented by the forced transition to RESCoversSpare with guard PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC >= 0.95, and its state action sends residual RES to Pspare.

Missing-required-grounding objection mapping: guard:OverloadBatteryLack is concretely represented by the forced transition to OverloadBatteryLack requiring demand above RES plus all thermal capacity, plus the added SoC and batt_Pmax suitability conditions. evidence.summary: The hard SL-7 unsafe_recovery finding is substantively repaired. In the old DSL, OverloadBatteryLack was entered whenever demand exceeded RES plus total thermal capacity and then computed Pbatt_discharge without checking battery suitability or discharge capacity. The candidate preserves the NL-required overload dispatch action but strengthens the OverloadBatteryLack forced-transition guard with SoC >= 0.2 and residual lack <= batt_Pmax, so the branch no longer permits unbounded or low-SoC battery discharge.

The candidate preserves the NL-required overload behavior: when extreme demand exceeds RES plus all thermal resources and the residual lack is battery-coverable, it activates LNG, eng3, DG1, and DG2, sets Pgen_req to total thermal capacity, sets Pbatt_discharge to the remaining lack, and leaves cmd_load_cut_in = 1 / cmd_load_cut_out = 0. This resolves the prior scenario regression in overload_activates_all_thermal_and_battery_lack, where the earlier rejected candidate had changed only the load commands to cut-out.

The diff does not drop NL-required states, inputs, outputs, dispatch branches, or command variables. All twelve states remain, including ZeroLoadCharge, ZeroLoadSpare, RESCoversCharge, RESCoversSpare, RESBatteryDischarge, LNG and diesel priority states, AllThermalWithinCapacity, and OverloadBatteryLack. Required variables PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, eng3_Pmax, Pgmax, Pd1max, Pgen_req, Pbatt_discharge, Pbatt_charge, Pspare, and generator/load command flags remain present.

The RES coverage obligations remain represented: RESCoversCharge is selected under PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC < 0.95 and charges residual renewable power; RESCoversSpare is selected under PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC >= 0.95 and sends residual renewable power to Pspare. These match the NL requirements for renewable coverage below and at/above the 0.95 SoC threshold.

The complete FixLog and repair_memory were considered. The first rejected candidate hash c442... caused a scenario regression by changing overload load commands to cut-out. The later candidate a3d... restored the scenario-required commands but local evidence still reported missing guard grounding. The current candidate has a new hash fa9a..., keeps the safety guard repair, preserves the restored load commands, and attempts to make the three required guard elements explicit with same-guard self-transitions while retaining the existing wildcard forced classification transitions.

local_override_rationale: Local check reports major drift with reason new_blocking_design_diagnostic; missing_required_grounding. The new design diagnostic is W_FORCED_OVERRIDES_NORMAL, complaining that the added RESCoversCharge -> RESCoversCharge, RESCoversSpare -> RESCoversSpare, and OverloadBatteryLack -> OverloadBatteryLack self-transitions duplicate the corresponding global forced classification transitions. This is a real redundancy introduced by the candidate, but it is not a semantic regression against the NL: the self-transitions have the same guards, no effects, and no enter/exit actions; the state during-actions remain the source of dispatch outputs. Because the forced transitions still perform the intended dynamic reclassification from any state, the duplicate self-transitions only add redundant local guard representation and do not alter required dispatch behavior.

Local check still reports missing_required_grounding for guard:RESCoversCharge, guard:RESCoversSpare, and guard:OverloadBatteryLack. I override this local rejection because the required guard semantics are concretely present in the DSL even if the local grounding matcher does not bind the abstract GroundingMap ids. guard:RESCoversCharge is represented by ! * -> RESCoversCharge with PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC < 0.95, plus the same guarded self-transition; guard:RESCoversSpare is represented by ! * -> RESCoversSpare with PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC >= 0.95, plus the same guarded self-transition; guard:OverloadBatteryLack is represented by ! * -> OverloadBatteryLack with demand above RES plus all thermal capacity, SoC >= 0.2, and residual lack <= batt_Pmax, plus the same guarded self-transition.

The repair_memory objection about the previous scenario_regression is resolved by the current candidate: OverloadBatteryLack again commands cmd_load_cut_in = 1 and cmd_load_cut_out = 0 while keeping all thermal cut-in commands and residual battery discharge. Local evidence for the current candidate reports regression_detected = false, so the prior failed scenario overload_activates_all_thermal_and_battery_lack is no longer an active regression.

The repair_memory objection about needing stronger grounding/override evidence is also resolved at this review level: SL-9 explicitly mapped each missing guard id to concrete DSL guards and actions, and this SL-10 decision provides the required structured override rationale for both local rejection kinds. The remaining local failure is therefore treated as conservative local grounding/design classification rather than evidence that an NL-required behavior is absent.

The new duplicate self-transition warning creates minor DSL drift, not major behavioral drift. It would be cleaner to remove the redundant self-transitions if the local grounding tool can be taught to recognize the existing forced guards, but accepting this candidate for the next full top-down revalidation is justified because the hard unsafe-recovery target is repaired, no NL-required element is dropped, and no scenario regression is currently reported.

decisions.rationale: Accepted. The request is rework-locked and the SL-7 unsafe_recovery finding remains valid: the original OverloadBatteryLack branch was entered for any demand above RES plus total thermal capacity and computed battery discharge without SoC or batt_Pmax suitability. The smallest safe DSL edit is to keep the NL-required overload dispatch action and scenario-required load service commands, but constrain the OverloadBatteryLack guard to suitable SoC and residual battery discharge within batt_Pmax. The latest SL-10 local objection is also addressed by removing the prior guarded self-transitions that caused W_FORCED_OVERRIDES_NORMAL duplicate forced/normal transitions. The required guard elements are intentionally represented by the existing NL-grounded wildcard forced guarded transitions, with explicit rationale for local_override rather than adding redundant normal self-transitions.

diff_summary.summary: Compared with the original DSL, only the OverloadBatteryLack forced-transition guard is strengthened with SoC >= 0.2 and residual battery-lack <= batt_Pmax. Overload load commands remain cmd_load_cut_in = 1 and cmd_load_cut_out = 0. scenario_results.description: default-init: with zero load, renewable production, and SoC below 0.95, the initial dispatch should land in ZeroLoadCharge and send RES power to battery charging.
scenario_results.name: default_init_zero_load_res_charges_battery

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: at PL=0 and SoC exactly 0.95, RES production should be classified as spare rather than battery charging.
scenario_results.name: zero_load_full_soc_spare_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when renewable power covers positive load and SoC is below 0.95, all load is served by RES and residual RES charges the battery.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_charge_below_full_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when renewable power covers positive load and SoC is exactly 0.95, residual RES should become spare power, not battery charge.
scenario_results.name: res_covers_spare_at_full_soc_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with RES below load, suitable SoC, and deficit exactly within battery capacity, battery discharge should cover the deficit before LNG or diesel.
scenario_results.name: battery_discharge_when_deficit_within_battery_capacity

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with low SoC and RES deficit, LNG should cut in and include the Pgmax/5 battery charging margin when that total fits LNG capacity.
scenario_results.name: lng_low_soc_pgmax_margin_within_capacity

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with suitable SoC but deficit above battery capacity and exactly within LNG capacity, LNG alone should cover the remaining demand.
scenario_results.name: lng_covers_deficit_after_battery_insufficient

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with low SoC, LNG margin over capacity, and LNG plus eng3 able to cover deficit plus Pd1max/10, LNG and eng3 should cut in and charge the battery margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_eng3_low_soc_pd1_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with suitable SoC and deficit above LNG alone but exactly within LNG plus eng3 capacity, LNG and eng3 should cover demand without DG1/DG2.
scenario_results.name: lng_eng3_covers_deficit_at_capacity_boundary

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with low SoC and deficit plus Pd1max/10 above LNG+eng3 but within LNG+eng3+DG1, DG1 should be used before DG2 and battery should receive the margin.
scenario_results.name: lng_eng3_dg1_low_soc_pd1_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: when deficit exceeds LNG+eng3 but is exactly within all thermal capacity, DG1 and DG2 should both cut in as last-priority units.
scenario_results.name: all_thermal_within_capacity_uses_dg2_last

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: for extreme demand above all RES and thermal resources, the overload lack branch should activate all thermal units and cover the remaining lack by battery discharge.
scenario_results.name: overload_activates_all_thermal_and_battery_lack

evidence: NL: "LNG before diesel units, and DG1/DG2 only as the last priority."
DSL has no separate DG1-only suitable-SoC state such as LNG+eng3+DG1 covers deficit.
DSL transition to AllThermalWithinCapacity: guard is `PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw < PL && PL - Ppv - Pw > LNG_Pmax + eng3_Pmax && PL - Ppv - Pw <= LNG_Pmax + eng3_Pmax + DG1_Pmax + DG2_Pmax`.
AllThermalWithinCapacity action sets `cmd_DG1_cut_in = 1` and `cmd_DG2_cut_in = 1`, so DG2 is activated even when `PL - Ppv - Pw <= LNG_Pmax + eng3_Pmax + DG1_Pmax`.
findings.summary: Thermal-unit priority is not faithfully modeled: the DSL cuts in DG2 for all deficits above LNG+eng3 capacity, even when DG1 alone could satisfy the remaining deficit.

evidence: NL: "The overload completion state is illegal" and "the state shall never occur in practice."
DSL defines `state OverloadBatteryLack` with normal during actions that activate all thermal units and keep load connected.
DSL has normal transitions from every listed state to OverloadBatteryLack when extreme demand exceeds thermal capacity and battery can cover the lack.

findings.summary: The overload state is treated as a reachable operational dispatch mode rather than an illegal/impossible state, and the oracle validates it as normal behavior.

evidence: DSL includes PV/WEC inputs `Ppv`, `Pw`, load `PL`, battery `SoC`, capacity variables, output powers, and cut-in/cut-out flags.
NL says the EMS returns requested generator power and issues cut-in/cut-out commands for generating units and loads.
DSL uses a single aggregate `Pgen_req` rather than per-unit requested power for LNG, eng3, DG1, and DG2.
DSL uses aggregate `cmd_load_cut_in` and `cmd_load_cut_out`; individual load classes or shedding priorities are not modeled.
findings.summary: Core components are represented, but dispatch is aggregated and load/generator commands are not decomposed by target power allocation.

latest_actionable_rework_guidance.summary: The hard NL/SL-7 target was unsafe recovery in OverloadBatteryLack: the original model entered the overload branch whenever demand exceeded RES plus all thermal capacity and computed Pbatt_discharge without SoC or batt_Pmax limits. The candidate strengthens every OverloadBatteryLack selection condition with SoC >= 0.2 and residual lack <= batt_Pmax, so the overload battery discharge action is no longer unbounded or entered without battery suitability/capacity checks.

The candidate preserves the NL-required overload dispatch behavior for the coverable emergency case: OverloadBatteryLack remains present, activates LNG, eng3, DG1, and DG2, sets Pgen_req to total thermal capacity, computes Pbatt_discharge as the residual lack, and preserves cmd_load_cut_in = 1 / cmd_load_cut_out = 0. This directly addresses the earlier scenario_regression in overload_activates_all_thermal_and_battery_lack where only load commands had mismatched expected 1/0 versus actual 0/1.

No NL-required states, variables, outputs, or dispatch actions are dropped. All twelve required states remain, including ZeroLoadCharge, ZeroLoadSpare, RESCoversCharge, RESCoversSpare, RESBatteryDischarge, LNG priority states, diesel priority states, AllThermalWithinCapacity, and OverloadBatteryLack. Required inputs PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, eng3_Pmax, Pgmax, Pd1max and required outputs Pgen_req, Pbatt_discharge, Pbatt_charge, Pspare plus generator/load command flags remain present.

evidence.summary: The SL-7 thermal-priority hard block is substantively resolved. The NL requires dispatch priority of RES first, batteries when suitable, LNG before diesel units, and DG1/DG2 only as last priority. The old DSL sent every suitable-SoC deficit above LNG+eng3 directly to AllThermalWithinCapacity and cut in both DG1 and DG2, even when DG1 alone could cover the remaining deficit. The candidate adds LNGEng3DG1CoversDeficit for PL > 0, RES below load, SoC >= 0.2, and deficit within LNG_Pmax + eng3_Pmax + DG1_Pmax; its action cuts in LNG, eng3, and DG1 while keeping DG2 cut out. AllThermalWithinCapacity is narrowed to deficits greater than LNG+eng3+DG1 and within LNG+eng3+DG1+DG2, so DG2 is only used when DG1 alone is insufficient.

The unsafe overload hard block remains repaired from prior accepted work. The candidate preserves the strengthened OverloadBatteryLack transition condition requiring demand above RES plus all thermal capacity, SoC >= 0.2, and residual lack <= batt_Pmax. This prevents the old unsafe behavior where the overload branch computed Pbatt_discharge without SoC suitability or battery discharge capacity limits.

The NL-required overload dispatch action is preserved for the coverable emergency case: OverloadBatteryLack still activates LNG, eng3, DG1, and DG2; sets Pgen_req to LNG_Pmax + eng3_Pmax + DG1_Pmax + DG2_Pmax; computes Pbatt_discharge as the remaining lack; sets Pbatt_charge = 0 and Pspare = 0; and preserves cmd_load_cut_in = 1 / cmd_load_cut_out = 0. This also preserves the prior scenario-regression fix where an earlier rejected candidate had incorrectly changed overload load commands to cut-out.

The NFRR quality-cap root causes identified in the request batch are addressed: missing DG1-only priority coverage is repaired, and overload reachability is constrained by battery suitability and capacity. The candidate also preserves the required states and variables from the grounding map, including ZeroLoadCharge, ZeroLoadSpare, RESCoversCharge, RESCoversSpare, RESBatteryDischarge, low-SoC charge-margin states, LNG/eng3 states, AllThermalWithinCapacity, OverloadBatteryLack, PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, eng3_Pmax, Pgmax, Pd1max, Pgen_req, Pbatt_discharge, Pbatt_charge, Pspare, and generator/load command flags.

The RES coverage obligations remain represented. RESCoversCharge is selected by normal guarded transitions under PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC < 0.95 and charges residual renewable power with Pbatt_charge = Ppv + Pw - PL. RESCoversSpare is selected under PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC >= 0.95 and sends residual renewable power to Pspare = Ppv + Pw - PL.

The complete FixLog and repair_memory were considered. Earlier candidates failed or required rework because c442 regressed overload load commands, fa9a introduced duplicate forced/normal self-transitions, and a3d relied on wildcard forced guard mappings that local checks still reported as missing grounding. The currently reviewed candidate builds on the previously accepted 813-style structure with concrete normal guard transitions and adds the DG1-only branch plus corresponding RES/overload transition sources, avoiding the known overload-command regression and avoiding the duplicate forced/normal self-transition pattern.

Local deterministic evidence reports no scenario_regression. The remaining local objections are structural/accounting diagnostics: forced_transition_count_drift old 108 to new 130 and missing_required_grounding for guard:RESCoversCharge, guard:RESCoversSpare, and guard:OverloadBatteryLack. These do not show a behavioral failure against the NL obligations or scenarios, and the DSL text contains concrete guarded transitions for each listed guard class.

local_override_rationale: Override for local rejection kind forced_transition_count_drift: the transition-count increase from 108 to 130 is an expected consequence of the NL-grounded repair, not accidental drift. The candidate adds one DG1-only dispatch state required to repair the SL-7 priority finding and adds corresponding guarded transition coverage from that new state to RESCoversCharge, RESCoversSpare, and OverloadBatteryLack so the already accepted concrete normal-transition grounding pattern remains complete for all dispatch states. The count increase is therefore tied to preserving global reselection behavior after the new DG1-only branch, not to unrelated model expansion.

Override for local rejection kind missing_required_grounding: the local checker still lists guard:RESCoversCharge, guard:RESCoversSpare, and guard:OverloadBatteryLack as missing, but the candidate DSL contains concrete normal guarded transitions for all three. guard:RESCoversCharge is represented by transitions from each concrete state, including LNGEng3DG1CoversDeficit, to RESCoversCharge with PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC < 0.95. guard:RESCoversSpare is represented by transitions from each concrete state to RESCoversSpare with PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC >= 0.95. guard:OverloadBatteryLack is represented by transitions from each concrete state to OverloadBatteryLack with demand above RES plus all thermal capacity, SoC >= 0.2, and residual lack <= batt_Pmax. These concrete guards directly implement the grounding-map obligations even though the local grounding matcher does not recognize them.

Override relative to repair_memory: the fa9a candidate attempted to satisfy missing grounding by adding normal self-transitions while retaining wildcard forced transitions, causing W_FORCED_OVERRIDES_NORMAL duplicate forced/normal diagnostics. The current candidate does not reintroduce that duplicate forced/normal self-transition pattern for the affected RES/overload guards. The a3d candidate repeated a prior hash and relied on wildcard forced guards; the current candidate is a substantive DSL change with explicit normal transitions and a new DG1-only branch. The earlier scenario regression involving overload load cut-in/cut-out is also not repeated because OverloadBatteryLack keeps cmd_load_cut_in = 1 and cmd_load_cut_out = 0.

Although the NL says there are twelve finite states and the candidate introduces an explicit DG1-only state, this addition is directly motivated by the hard NL-priority finding that DG2 must not be cut in when DG1 alone satisfies the deficit. The candidate preserves all originally grounded required states and should proceed to full top-down revalidation where the state-count abstraction can be reviewed in context; it is not a reason to block this repair handoff because the requested hard-blocking priority behavior cannot be represented by the prior AllThermalWithinCapacity action without prematurely cutting in DG2.

evidence.summary: The SL-7 thermal-priority hard block is substantively resolved. The NL requires dispatch priority of RES first, batteries when suitable, LNG before diesel units, and DG1/DG2 only as last priority. The old DSL sent every suitable-SoC deficit above LNG+eng3 directly to AllThermalWithinCapacity and cut in both DG1 and DG2, even when DG1 alone could cover the remaining deficit. The candidate adds LNGEng3DG1CoversDeficit for PL > 0, RES below load, SoC >= 0.2, and deficit within LNG_Pmax + eng3_Pmax + DG1_Pmax; its action cuts in LNG, eng3, and DG1 while keeping DG2 cut out. AllThermalWithinCapacity is narrowed to deficits greater than LNG+eng3+DG1 and within LNG+eng3+DG1+DG2, so DG2 is only used when DG1 alone is insufficient.

The unsafe overload hard block remains repaired from prior accepted work. The candidate preserves the strengthened OverloadBatteryLack transition condition requiring demand above RES plus all thermal capacity, SoC >= 0.2, and residual lack <= batt_Pmax. This prevents the old unsafe behavior where the overload branch computed Pbatt_discharge without SoC suitability or battery discharge capacity limits.

The NL-required overload dispatch action is preserved for the coverable emergency case: OverloadBatteryLack still activates LNG, eng3, DG1, and DG2; sets Pgen_req to LNG_Pmax + eng3_Pmax + DG1_Pmax + DG2_Pmax; computes Pbatt_discharge as the remaining lack; sets Pbatt_charge = 0 and Pspare = 0; and preserves cmd_load_cut_in = 1 / cmd_load_cut_out = 0. This also preserves the prior scenario-regression fix where an earlier rejected candidate had incorrectly changed overload load commands to cut-out.

The NFRR quality-cap root causes identified in the request batch are addressed: missing DG1-only priority coverage is repaired, and overload reachability is constrained by battery suitability and capacity. The candidate also preserves the required states and variables from the grounding map, including ZeroLoadCharge, ZeroLoadSpare, RESCoversCharge, RESCoversSpare, RESBatteryDischarge, low-SoC charge-margin states, LNG/eng3 states, AllThermalWithinCapacity, OverloadBatteryLack, PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, eng3_Pmax, Pgmax, Pd1max, Pgen_req, Pbatt_discharge, Pbatt_charge, Pspare, and generator/load command flags.

The RES coverage obligations remain represented. RESCoversCharge is selected by normal guarded transitions under PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC < 0.95 and charges residual renewable power with Pbatt_charge = Ppv + Pw - PL. RESCoversSpare is selected under PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC >= 0.95 and sends residual renewable power to Pspare = Ppv + Pw - PL.

local_override_rationale: Override for local rejection kind forced_transition_count_drift: the transition-count increase from 108 to 130 is an expected consequence of the NL-grounded repair, not accidental drift. The candidate adds one DG1-only dispatch state required to repair the SL-7 priority finding and adds corresponding guarded transition coverage from that new state to RESCoversCharge, RESCoversSpare, and OverloadBatteryLack so the already accepted concrete normal-transition grounding pattern remains complete for all dispatch states. The count increase is therefore tied to preserving global reselection behavior after the new DG1-only branch, not to unrelated model expansion.

Override for local rejection kind missing_required_grounding: the local checker still lists guard:RESCoversCharge, guard:RESCoversSpare, and guard:OverloadBatteryLack as missing, but the candidate DSL contains concrete normal guarded transitions for all three. guard:RESCoversCharge is represented by transitions from each concrete state, including LNGEng3DG1CoversDeficit, to RESCoversCharge with PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC < 0.95. guard:RESCoversSpare is represented by transitions from each concrete state to RESCoversSpare with PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC >= 0.95. guard:OverloadBatteryLack is represented by transitions from each concrete state to OverloadBatteryLack with demand above RES plus all thermal capacity, SoC >= 0.2, and residual lack <= batt_Pmax. These concrete guards directly implement the grounding-map obligations even though the local grounding matcher does not recognize them.

Override relative to repair_memory: the fa9a candidate attempted to satisfy missing grounding by adding normal self-transitions while retaining wildcard forced transitions, causing W_FORCED_OVERRIDES_NORMAL duplicate forced/normal diagnostics. The current candidate does not reintroduce that duplicate forced/normal self-transition pattern for the affected RES/overload guards. The a3d candidate repeated a prior hash and relied on wildcard forced guards; the current candidate is a substantive DSL change with explicit normal transitions and a new DG1-only branch. The earlier scenario regression involving overload load cut-in/cut-out is also not repeated because OverloadBatteryLack keeps cmd_load_cut_in = 1 and cmd_load_cut_out = 0.

Although the NL says there are twelve finite states and the candidate introduces an explicit DG1-only state, this addition is directly motivated by the hard NL-priority finding that DG2 must not be cut in when DG1 alone satisfies the deficit. The candidate preserves all originally grounded required states and should proceed to full top-down revalidation where the state-count abstraction can be reviewed in context; it is not a reason to block this repair handoff because the requested hard-blocking priority behavior cannot be represented by the prior AllThermalWithinCapacity action without prematurely cutting in DG2.

repair_rationale: Thermal priority repair: LNGEng3DG1CoversDeficit is added for the suitable-SoC range where LNG plus eng3 plus DG1 can satisfy the deficit. Its action cuts in LNG, eng3, and DG1 while keeping DG2 cut out, so DG2 is no longer used prematurely.

AllThermalWithinCapacity is narrowed to deficits greater than LNG_Pmax + eng3_Pmax + DG1_Pmax and within LNG_Pmax + eng3_Pmax + DG1_Pmax + DG2_Pmax, so DG2 is reserved for the final thermal-capacity priority tier.

Unsafe overload repair is preserved: every OverloadBatteryLack normal guard requires demand above total thermal capacity, SoC >= 0.2, and residual lack <= batt_Pmax. This prevents unbounded or low-SoC battery-discharge entry while preserving the NL-required all-thermal plus battery-lack dispatch for the coverable emergency case.

Required grounding retained: guard:RESCoversCharge remains concretely represented by normal guarded transitions to RESCoversCharge with PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC < 0.95 and the state charges residual renewable power.

Required grounding retained: guard:RESCoversSpare remains concretely represented by normal guarded transitions to RESCoversSpare with PL > 0 && Ppv + Pw >= PL && SoC >= 0.95 and the state sends residual renewable power to Pspare.

Required grounding retained: guard:OverloadBatteryLack remains concretely represented by normal guarded transitions to OverloadBatteryLack with the strengthened SoC and batt_Pmax suitability checks, and action:OverloadBatteryLackDispatch remains concrete.

evidence.summary: The candidate partially addresses the SL-7 illegal-state concern by adding overload_illegal and removing normal incoming transitions to OverloadBatteryLack, but it over-corrects and drops an NL-required overload behavior. The NL requires that when extreme demand exceeds RES and thermal resources, the EMS activates all thermal generating units and covers the lack by battery discharge, while also treating that completion state as illegal/should-not-occur in practice. Making OverloadBatteryLack unreachable removes the runtime dispatch path for that stated emergency branch.

Local deterministic evidence reports a real scenario regression, not merely conservative grounding drift. Scenario wrong_target_probe_lng_to_overload_lack starts in LNGCoversDeficit with PL=220, Ppv=10, Pw=10, SoC=0.5, batt_Pmax=100, LNG_Pmax=80, eng3_Pmax=30, DG1_Pmax=30, DG2_Pmax=20. Expected step 0 target is LNGShipEMS.OverloadBatteryLack with Pgen_req=160, Pbatt_discharge=40, Pbatt_charge=0, Pspare=0, all thermal cut-in commands set to 1/0, and cmd_load_cut_in=1/cmd_load_cut_out=0. Actual state remains LNGShipEMS.LNGCoversDeficit, so the overload dispatch action is not reached.

The new W_UNREACHABLE_STATE diagnostic is directly caused by the DSL diff: all normal incoming transitions from concrete dispatch states to OverloadBatteryLack were removed, leaving only an OverloadBatteryLack self-loop. Because the state is required by the grounding map and its dispatch action is required, this is not an acceptable dead-state representation.

The FixLog repair memory shows prior acceptable direction: preserve OverloadBatteryLack dispatch, preserve cmd_load_cut_in=1/cmd_load_cut_out=0, and constrain overload selection with SoC >= 0.2 and residual lack <= batt_Pmax. The current candidate preserves the commands but regresses reachability and therefore breaks the previously passing overload scenario obligation.

The candidate also continues to trigger missing_required_grounding for guard:RESCoversCharge, guard:RESCoversSpare, and guard:OverloadBatteryLack. RES guards appear textually present, but the overload guard is now only a self-loop on an unreachable state, which is not sufficient concrete runtime grounding for the required overload branch.

rework_instructions: Restore concrete guarded inbound transitions from normal dispatch states to OverloadBatteryLack for the strengthened overload condition: PL > 0, Ppv + Pw < PL, PL - Ppv - Pw > LNG_Pmax + eng3_Pmax + DG1_Pmax + DG2_Pmax, SoC >= 0.2, and residual lack <= batt_Pmax. Do not rely on an OverloadBatteryLack self-loop to ground this guard.

Keep overload_illegal as an explicit illegal-state marker, but make it coexist with the required emergency dispatch path. OverloadBatteryLack.enter may set overload_illegal = 1, and/or the restored inbound transitions may set overload_illegal = 1 in an effect block if the DSL supports effects.

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: from a concrete thermal leaf, PL=0 with SoC at 0.95 must target ZeroLoadSpare, catching wrong-target mutations of the zero-load full-SoC branch.
scenario_results.name: wrong_target_probe_thermal_to_zero_load_spare

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: from ZeroLoadCharge, low SoC and a deficit plus Pgmax/5 exactly within LNG capacity must target LNGLowSoCChargeMargin.
scenario_results.name: wrong_target_probe_zero_load_to_lng_low_soc_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: from ZeroLoadSpare, low SoC with LNG margin over LNG capacity but Pd1max/10 margin within LNG+eng3 must target LNGEng3LowSoCChargeMargin.
scenario_results.name: wrong_target_probe_zero_load_spare_to_lng_eng3_low_soc_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: from RESCoversSpare, low SoC with deficit plus Pd1max/10 within LNG+eng3+DG1 must target LNGEng3DG1LowSoCChargeMargin and keep DG2 out.
scenario_results.name: wrong_target_probe_res_spare_to_dg1_low_soc_margin

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: from OverloadBatteryLack, suitable-SoC deficit above LNG+eng3 but within LNG+eng3+DG1 must target LNGEng3DG1CoversDeficit, not AllThermalWithinCapacity.
scenario_results.name: wrong_target_probe_overload_to_dg1_suitable_soc

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: from RESCoversCharge, suitable-SoC deficit above LNG+eng3+DG1 but exactly within all thermal capacity must target AllThermalWithinCapacity.
scenario_results.name: wrong_target_probe_res_charge_to_all_thermal

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: from LNGCoversDeficit, extreme demand above all thermal capacity but within battery lack coverage must target OverloadBatteryLack.
scenario_results.name: wrong_target_probe_lng_to_overload_lack

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: from RESBatteryDischarge, suitable-SoC deficit above LNG alone but exactly within LNG+eng3 must target LNGEng3CoversDeficit.
scenario_results.name: wrong_target_probe_battery_to_lng_eng3_suitable_soc

scenario_results.description: default-init: first cycle must dispatch the root initial transition to ZeroLoadCharge and charge batteries from RES when PL=0 and SoC is below 0.95.
scenario_results.name: default_init_zero_load_charge_dispatch

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: from RESBatteryDischarge, a zero-load low-SoC condition must be globally reselected to ZeroLoadCharge, exposing deletion of the wildcard forced zero-load charge transition.
scenario_results.name: missing_forced_probe_battery_to_zero_load_charge

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: at the exact SoC=0.95 RES-covered threshold, the EMS must treat residual renewable power as spare, catching high-threshold or unreachable-target mutations.
scenario_results.name: boundary_soc_095_res_cover_spare

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: with suitable SoC and deficit exactly equal to batt_Pmax, the EMS must use battery discharge rather than LNG, catching capacity-threshold and unreachable-target mutations.
scenario_results.name: boundary_battery_deficit_equals_batt_pmax

evidence: DSL declares PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, batt_Pmax, LNG_Pmax, eng3_Pmax, DG1_Pmax, DG2_Pmax, Pgmax, Pd1max, Pgen_req, Pbatt_discharge, Pbatt_charge, Pspare, generator cut-in/cut-out flags, load cut-in/cut-out flags, and overload_illegal.
DSL includes RES coverage, battery discharge, LNG, LNG+eng3, LNG+eng3+DG1, all-thermal, zero-load, and overload states.
sim_summary reports 14/14 scenarios passed, including DG1-only suitable-SoC and low-SoC probes.
findings.summary: The candidate covers the main NL components and the repaired DG1-only dispatch branch; required inputs, dispatch outputs, generator/load command flags, and operating states are present.

evidence: NL: "The twelve finite states are selected by logical transition conditions..."
inspect_model_to_json_summary.metrics.n_states_leaf is 13.
DSL includes both LNGEng3DG1LowSoCChargeMargin and LNGEng3DG1CoversDeficit in addition to AllThermalWithinCapacity and OverloadBatteryLack.
findings.summary: There is a mild state-count/name fidelity drift: the NL says twelve finite states, while the inspected model has 13 leaf states. The extra DG1-only suitable-SoC branch appears priority-justified but still deviates from the literal count.

evidence: Top-level forced transitions include ZeroLoadCharge, ZeroLoadSpare, RESBatteryDischarge, low-SoC and thermal deficit states, and AllThermalWithinCapacity, but not RESCoversCharge, RESCoversSpare, or OverloadBatteryLack.

Grounding update hints report remaining local missing_required_grounding for guard:RESCoversCharge, guard:RESCoversSpare, and guard:OverloadBatteryLack, while noting textual guarded transitions exist.
[*] -> ZeroLoadCharge is unconditional.
findings.summary: The RES-covered and overload guard grounding remains structurally uneven: RES charge/spare and overload are represented by many concrete normal transitions rather than the same top-level forced-selection pattern used for most deficit branches, leaving a small initial-cycle/grounding accounting risk.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary.metrics.n_events is 0.
inspect_model_to_json_summary.metrics.n_transitions_forced is 130 and n_transitions_normal is 40.
Grounding assumptions state the model dynamically reselects the applicable dispatch state from current inputs rather than preserving mode memory.
Most guards are direct predicates over PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and capacity bounds.
findings.summary: The model is largely a condition-classification table rather than a stateful EMS controller with temporal mode memory.

evidence: NL: "The overload completion state is illegal... and the state shall never occur in practice."
DSL state OverloadBatteryLack has enter { overload_illegal = 1; } and during actions that command all thermal units and load served.
sim_summary scenario wrong_target_probe_lng_to_overload_lack passes with actual_state LNGShipEMS.OverloadBatteryLack and overload_illegal = 1.
findings.summary: The illegal overload branch is reachable and validated as expected behavior. The DSL does mark overload_illegal, but it otherwise treats the illegal state as an operational dispatch state; this should be retained only if the intended interpretation is diagnostic modeling of an impossible/extreme condition.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary.transition_count is 170.
design_diagnostics_summary reports advisory_count 376 and blocking_count 0.
Diagnostic inventory includes many W_DURING_CONST_ASSIGN and W_GUARD_VARS_NEVER_CHANGE warnings.
inspect_model_to_json_summary.metrics.var_to_leaf_ratio is 2.0.
findings.summary: The implementation has high transition and warning density consistent with a generated dispatch table, but current diagnostics are advisory rather than deterministic blockers.

evidence: Grounding update hints state the current candidate preserves required states, variables, and actions.
design_diagnostics_summary.blocking_count is 0 and warning_budget_exhausted is empty.
The DSL retains OverloadBatteryLack and required dispatch actions instead of removing them to avoid warnings.
findings.summary: No clear unjustified warning-suppression repair is present in the current candidate; prior loop hints indicate repairs were aimed at DG1-only coverage and overload reachability rather than deleting required behavior to silence diagnostics.

evidence: Model has 13 leaf states, 26 variables, 170 transitions, and state actions for dispatch outputs and commands.
sim_summary passes 14/14 scenarios.
Remaining concerns are mostly advisory structure/grounding risks, synthesized thresholds, and condition-table style rather than missing core DSL content.
findings.summary: Estimated NFRR tier is T2 within-scope candidate, possibly approaching T3 after deterministic review, with no T0/T1 quality cap. The model is not an empty shell and covers the main required states, guards, and actions, but simplification and grounding assumptions prevent signed-reference confidence.
